title: A Process Made for Mars is Now Uncovering Ancient Art on Earth - Nautilus
gist: The decorrelation stretch image-processing technique, originally developed by NASA to enhance satellite and Mars imagery, is now used to reveal hidden cave art and can run on a phone.

insights.claim: Decorrelation stretch, an image-processing method developed by NASA scientists to extract detail from satellite imagery including photos of Mars, is now being used to reveal hidden cave art on Earth.

insights.so_what: Example of space-program R&D spillover into cultural heritage and imaging software.

insights.claim: Decorrelation stretch works as a high-powered contrast enhancer, remapping colors across a wider range of shades so that a faint red and slightly darker red can become bright red and bright green.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Commodity computational-imaging techniques create low-cost tools for archaeology and inspection use cases.

insights.claim: The decorrelation stretch technique can be run on an ordinary smartphone, democratizing a formerly specialist NASA imaging tool.
